en: cook egg slowly in a pan

does: Sets beaten egg mixed with cooked vegetables or cheese slowly in a frying pan over low heat, without stirring, into a thick flat cake that is turned once.

intro.what: A frittata is set slowly, flat, and never stirred.
intro.why: Low heat sets the thick cake right through while the base turns just golden, not brown and rubbery.

how: Have the filling cooked and spread evenly in an oiled pan.
Pour in the beaten egg and turn the heat to low.
Leave it alone. Run a spatula round the edge now and then and tilt the pan so a little loose egg runs under.
When the base and the edges are set and only the top is runny, turn it over with a plate, or finish the top under a grill.

cues.text: The edges are set and pulling away from the pan and only a thin layer on top still shines.
A gentle smell of browning egg, never of burning.

mistakes.mistake: Too high a heat, so the base burns before the middle sets.
Stirring the egg, so it turns into scrambled egg.
mistakes.fix: Leave it to set in one piece.

quiz.question: Why is a frittata cooked on low heat?
choices: So the middle sets before the base burns.
So it rises like a soufflé.
So the cheese does not melt.
quiz.because: A thick egg cake needs time to set through.

quiz.question: What do you do while it cooks?
choices: Leave it, loosening the edge now and then.

quiz.question: When is it ready to turn?
choices: When it is still liquid all through.
When the edges and base are set and only the top is runny.
quiz.because: Turn it when only the top is still loose.

quiz.question: The base was dark and the middle still raw. What would you change?
choices: Cook it on a lower heat for longer.
quiz.because: Slow heat evens out the cooking.

comes_after.why: The eggs are beaten before they go into the pan.
